findings.evidence: The statement assumes a “C^1 local diffeomorphism,” but the cited definition defines local diffeomorphisms only for smooth maps. If the intended meaning is a C^1 map with C^1 local inverse, that notion and its local inverse result are not stated among this item’s prerequisites. Define and cite that notion, or state the smooth premise. This is a suspected mismatch, not a counterexample to the intended claim.

Step 3.1 takes a countable union of Euclidean null sets and says “Countable subadditivity makes it null.” The item does not establish or cite countable-union closure for Euclidean nullity. Under the given AC_omega, add the cube-cover argument using budgets epsilon*2^(-i-1), or cite/add lem-null-sets-in-rn-closed-under-subsets-and-countable-unions.

The step converts surjectivity on T_yN/T_yZ to surjectivity of dh_y composed with dF_p after asserting ker(dh_y)=T_yZ. That kernel identity follows from the regular-level tangent-space result [L3], but Step 2.1 does not cite or use it. Add the tangent-kernel step and identify the induced quotient map T_yN/T_yZ -> R^c as an isomorphism.

The cited slicing lemma requires a compact set contained in [a,b] x R^(n-1), but the proof applies it directly to the compact image f(C_0 intersect closure(B)). Choose a compact interval containing that image’s first-coordinate projection, and handle an empty image separately, to meet the lemma’s hypothesis.

The proof applies Morse–Sard to pi_S:W -> S, but establishes only that W=F^{-1}(Z) is embedded; it does not establish that the restricted product projection pi_S is smooth. State that the inclusion W -> M x S is smooth and compose it with the smooth product projection, or verify smoothness in slice charts before applying Sard.
The tag text [L1, given, algebra] is inserted between the prose and the displayed matrix, then repeated at the end of the step. Keep one valid tag clause after the completed step’s punctuation.

The statement fixes one arbitrary q and proves that q is a regular value after generic translation. The title says “every point” and “zero”; Proof 3.1 also calls the chosen value a transverse zero, although q need not be 0 and no one translation is shown to work for every target value. Narrow the title and wording to the fixed value q.
